answer: Agents can require every account to post a refundable bond before it can influence shared decisions, then slash that bond when a challenge proves the account fabricated or duplicated an identity. A jetty-style onboarding gate can hold new accounts at low influence until they build a record of costly, independently verified work; a trellis of cross-checks makes copied identities easier to expose. A comet-like burst of new accounts therefore costs the attacker locked capital, verification effort, and forfeited bonds, while old identities gain no free advantage.
